Read `README.md` and current rollout evidence first. Produce exactly one multi-wake target-policy candidate in `solver/`. Keep candidate-specific reasoning in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`, and add or materially revise at least one evidence-backed reusable lesson in `guidance/control_experience.md` from the assigned parent, sampled solver results, and inherited logs. If no positive lesson survives the evidence, record a concrete negative result and what later workers should avoid or test. The candidate is incomplete until both files are updated. Work only inside this Phase 2 workspace.

Use the fish-control bookshelf through this structured transfer protocol:

1. Before the first architecture proposal from the common naive seed, consult `guidance/skills/fish-control-primitives/SKILL.md` and its references.
2. On later iterations, consult it again when the inherited guidance indicates three consecutive completed iterations with neither a new controller mechanism nor a semantic improvement such as a new success, a better termination class, or a meaningfully different useful trajectory.
3. Consultation is required at those moments; adopting a primitive is optional. Do not use the shelf to justify scalar-only gain tuning.
4. If a source informs the edit, record a concise block in `logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md`:

```text
bookshelf_consulted: true
source_domain:
source_mechanism:
transferable_invariant:
nontransferable_details:
policy_translation:
falsification:
```

Translate only the invariant into normalized body-frame observations and the two-joint state-feedback contract. Prefer one mechanism or one small compatible combination. Published gains, species-specific kinematics, exact vortex phases, and task-specific routes are not transferable answers.

I’ll first read the workspace contract and inspect the current rollout artifacts, then I’ll consult the required fish-control bookshelf before deciding whether the policy needs a new mechanism or an evidence-led refinement. I’ll keep all edits within this Phase 2 workspace.

I’m using two workspace skills here: the visual-evidence skill because policy edits must be grounded in both 3D wake views, and the fish-control-primitives skill because this is the required bookshelf consultation point. I’ll read both instruction sets completely before acting on the evidence.

The sampled set is unusually narrow: all four formal examples are captures, so there is no sampled failure sheet to compare visually. I’ll treat the best-score capture and the current prefill as the strongest available contrast, then use the inherited failure summaries only as negative boundaries—not as unseen visual evidence.

The evidence already rules out a tempting direction: an inherited coupled allocator reduced clipping but lost the target route, so I’m treating lower saturation as non-improvement unless capture and the route band survive. I’m now quantifying where the successful carrier actually has residual error, so the candidate can change one observable mechanism rather than add another broad recovery stack.

The useful residual is now concrete: across all four captures, one-cycle rigid-heading residual is about `-0.65 ×` anterior-joint displacement with correlation near `-0.95`; the raw body-lateral route request therefore carries a strong beat-frequency component. I’ll test one compact mechanism—partial displacement-based compensation of the target body axis—while leaving the proven oscillator, mean-curvature shares, half-cycle allocation, posterior lag, and hard projection intact.

The candidate and durable guidance are now updated. The guidance records the inherited allocator as a concrete negative result and treats phase compensation only as a falsifiable observation ablation—not as a same-worker success. I’m moving through contract/schema checks now, then I’ll invoke the mandated check-runner without running CFD.

The required check-runner is now being invoked from its workspace configuration. It will run the semantic-guidance check, the lightweight Julia policy/schema contract, and the solver boundary audit only; no CFD.

A supplemental local Julia fuzz check cannot start because this shell has no `julia` executable on `PATH`; that is an environment issue, not a policy assertion failure. The mandated runner is still checking the configured commands, and I’ll use its result to determine whether an alternate installed Julia path exists or whether only the Python/static checks can be completed here.

The mandated runner passed guidance provenance and the solver boundary. Its only failure was the missing `julia` name on `PATH`; I located the installed Julia 1.12.6 binary and will rerun the full runner with that directory prepended. The runner also normalized the duplicated assigned-parent marker in `README.md`, which was necessary for the provenance checker to resolve the parent.

Produced exactly one candidate: bounded anterior-displacement compensation removes beat-synchronous body-axis motion from the route signal while preserving the proven propulsion and steering carrier.

- [Candidate policy](solver/cases/dogfish_3d_shape_policy/candidate_target_policy.jl:1)
- [Evidence and bookshelf transfer notes](logs/optimize/wake_policy_notes.md:1)
- [Reusable guidance lessons](guidance/control_experience.md:71)

The mandated check-runner passed all three checks: guidance semantic change, Julia policy/schema contract, and solver boundary audit. It also removed the duplicate assigned-parent marker from `README.md` so provenance validation could resolve correctly. No CFD was run.
